title: Deployment stopgap procedures and risk communications kit
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Create a compact, actionable bundle of stopgap procedures, rollback scripts, and communication templates for high-risk launches. Scope: hosted API and Dedicated flows for runtime-1.22; excludes long-lived private deployments (handled by Private team). Deliverables: 1) short runbook (<= 2 pages) with decision ladder and rollback checklist, 2) three templated messages (incident start, rollback confirm, postmortem invite), 3) owner matrix and on-call escalation map, 4) validated rollback smoke plan in staging and one dry-run on Dedicated cluster. Goals: minimize time-to-decision during degradations, ensure consistent cross-team comms, and reduce mean time-to-recover (MTTR) by 35% for P0s originating in runtime surface.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook published to Confluence and linked in the release notes
Rollback checklist runs end-to-end in staging without errors (dry-run evidence: CI job log)
Communication templates approved by legal and comms teams
On-call rotation owners and escalation phone/Slack blocks verified
At least one rehearsal executed with ENG, SRE, PM, and Support prior to cutover
comms_templates:
INCIDENT START (short):
Subject: [P0] runtime-1.22 degradation — initial alert
Channel: #launch-watchtower and #sre-oncall
Body: TL;DR: We are investigating an elevated error rate for text-generation endpoints affecting ~X% of requests. Current impact: increased 5xx rate, latency spikes. Action being taken: throttling non-critical background jobs, routing traffic to fallback model variant, initiating rollback contingency evaluation. Owners: ENG oncall (Leo Martinez), SRE (Priya Singh), PM (Asha Patel). Next update: 15min. Links: <dashboard>, <runbook>.

ROLLBACK CONFIRM (post-decision):
Subject: [ACTION] runtime-1.22 rollback initiated
Channel: #launch-watchtower, pagerduty notify, email to stakeholders
Body: We have initiated a rollback to runtime-1.21 due to sustained degradation on runtime-1.22. Expected timeline: 12-20 min for traffic drain and verification. User-facing impact: brief request routing changes; no data loss expected. Verification steps: health-checks green across all regions, canary pass, consumer metrics stabilizing. Rollback owner: ENG release lead (name), SRE lead (name). If you see any anomalies after rollback, escalate to the SRE pager.

POST-INCIDENT DEBRIEF (template):
Subject: Postmortem: runtime-1.22 incident [P0] — summary and actions
To: release-owners, eng-leads, product, support, legal
Body: One-paragraph summary, timeline with key decision points, root cause hypothesis, immediate mitigations applied, long-term remediation plan with owners and ETA, and checklist for re-release prerequisites. Meeting request: schedule 72 hours from incident close for a 60-min blameless review. Attach: logs, rollback verification checklist, pagerduty incident link.
owner_matrix: ENG release lead: Leo Martinez — decision authority for rollback
SRE lead: Priya Singh — rollback execution and verification
PM owner: Asha Patel — stakeholder comms and release hold decisions
Support lead: Carmen Liu — customer comms & triage
Legal/comms: Samir Rao — message approval for external customers
escalation_path: If unresolved after 20 min: escalate to SRE lead (Priya) and PM (Asha)
If service remains degraded after 40 min: executive notify (CTO, Head of Product)
operational_triggers: Canary fail rate > 2.5x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes -> start incident
Global 5xx rate > 1% and user-facing latency > 2s for 10 minutes -> evaluate rollback
Observed data loss or integrity issue -> immediate rollback and P0 escalation
validation_plan: Run smoke rollback in staging using infra/rollback.sh (CI job: rollback-smoke-runtime-1.22)
Execute one dry-run on Dedicated in a non-production pool during maintenance window
Monitor canary dashboard and synthetic traces during dry-run and collect screenshots/logs
risk_tradeoffs: Full rollback reduces exposure quickly but may mask underlying performance regressions — require post-rollback root cause analysis
Canary-only mitigation reduces blast radius but may not cover systemic runtime-level regressions
Temporary throttling of background workloads reduces latency but can delay downstream batch processes
qa_checklist: QA sign-off on rollback smoke run (QA engineer: Jordan Kim)
Regression scans for tokenization and KV-cache correctness post-rollback
Sanity checks for API contract compatibility (embedding shapes, chat tool-calls)
release_notes_coordination: Add a 'Known Risks & Contingencies' section to runtime-1.22 release notes with links to runbook
Notify top 20 customers via targeted email if rollback occurs; draft prepared in comms_templates
Post-release: add an entry in the release changelog referencing the incident ticket
